- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.0+ sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves when sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.5+ sentiment) — model misses tail risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in early days of strong sentiment shifts — adjust for momentum lag (e.g., 1–2 days delay in reacting to sentiment spikes).
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.5), model often overestimates — apply downward bias correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overcorrects after recent highs — reduce forecast peak by 1–2% if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model should not forecast upward trend — force mean reversion toward recent 10-day average.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed (e.g., +0.3 to -0.5) — model overconfident in directionality.
